title: Prove polynomial bit bounds for complete inverse-circuit certificates
body:
Prove polynomial rational size and bit cost for the complete inverse-circuit certificate producer and its separately transcribed checker. The source already bounds field operations; this result also bounds the numerators, denominators and elimination coordinates. Both equality certificates and shortest nonzero coefficient words have polynomial encoding size. This closes the producer-size gap before the orthogonal-witness and funded-detector interfaces. The complete kappa calculation and selected frontier remain unchanged.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/PROOF.md), [budget calculator and exact audit](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/budget.py), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/RESULT.json), and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/SOURCES.json) define the result.

The contract retains all independent inputs and returned roles, old values on aliased queries, and true named-generator inverses. Inputs use explicit integers or integer/fraction strings; unreduced operands are charged. The new budget interface rejects compressed decimal/exponent syntax before expansion. The upstream parser is unchanged. The theorem covers this explicit rational encoding, with Python's integer-string limit disabled by the standard per-process option below.

For D=r+q, a common denominator and scalar-gain bound control the compiled matrices. Scale every candidate path row to one integer lattice. Pivot minors then bound the normalized echelon rows, their original-row coordinates and every closure coefficient. A separate bound includes unreduced arithmetic temporaries. These steps convert the existing field-operation count into a polynomial bit-time and space bound. The bounds are conservative; this is neither a practical speedup nor an optimal-size result.

@krzysztofwojt supplied the compiler, reachable-basis search, independent checker, exact oracles and shortest-word theorem in [PR #5262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5262), consumed at `6f92ccf1e61c4668c8ee687bd1df8b42932b8759`. Those files are unchanged. The [retained source proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/vendor/UPSTREAM-PROOF.md) preserves @zxv's [PR #5235](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5235), the dirty-echo/tensor/phase lineage and classical Magnus, rational-series and weighted-automata credit. Cramer's rule, determinant height bounds and polynomial exact linear algebra are classical. No new general equivalence algorithm or global literature priority is claimed.

Ali Romman's [PR #5315](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5315), head `9bebc267c4608e51fcc94a543b8e0d66077cdfbb`, supplies the orthogonal construction; [PR #5339](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5339), head `26fe40cbca6972a0e392e9248a9cb8a84368530b`, supplies the detector bound after the word is given. Their [orthogonal proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/vendor/ORTHOGONAL-PROOF.md) and [precision proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4/research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds/vendor/PRECISION-PROOF.md) are retained for the composition corollary. Their full replays were not rerun in this package. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

Base: current main `ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf`, priority revision 7. Eleven consumed files are retained byte-exact at ancestor `5fb9c3ee9a4073b7085d7b5b8e7d8f524e1e520c`. The replay does not need unmerged upstream Git objects.

Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/inverse-certificate-bit-bounds
```

The registered normal and optimized commands include `-X int_max_str_digits=0` and both pass with `PASS_INVERSE_CERTIFICATE_BIT_BOUNDS`. All 99 programs pass: 36 equality certificates, 63 nonzero words, 98 independent reduced-word comparisons and 63 exact matrix witnesses. Cases include a 16,001-bit scalar, large unreduced fractions, coprime denominators, near dependencies, delayed inverse tails, dirty returns and aliases. The weighted 2^64-word case uses 260 states and 64 invariant rows; its certificate coefficients need at most 254 bits. Nine controls and three separate edge audits pass. Four actual code mutations fail in both modes for mathematical reasons.

Committed bytes, every declared source pin's direct ancestry, official export integrity and both read-only Git-free replays pass; all 21 exported files remain unchanged. The full-history wrapper is unpassed in this shallow checkout. No independent human/proof-kernel review, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, native tape or complete compiler/kappa calculation was run. A native adapter still needs one pinned caller with all extra operator relations, types, phases, storage and paid-call costs. Polynomial certificate size does not supply that admission.

Hosted [run 40002911314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40002911314) passed planning and the registered Linux replay for published head `b6a8111fe26b2ab4eb24d56f46ae0da3ec7182e4`. Hosted execution is separate from independent scientific review.
